summary: Reviewed 2 modified files: mcp-server/gui/api.ts (handlePromoteKnowledge ~L1862, handleMoveKnowledge ~L1960, KnowledgeMoveBodySchema ~L1931) and mcp-server/tests/gui/api-knowledge.test.ts. Also reviewed supporting files: src/schema/knowledge.ts, src/storage/knowledge-store.ts, and gui/server.ts. 0 Critical, 0 High, 1 Medium, 2 Low, 2 Info findings. Security sign-off: PASS. Note: routes are not yet wired into server.ts (deferred to WP-002) — the handlers are pure business logic; the routing-layer controls apply to the existing knowledge endpoints.

comments.note: A01 (Broken Access Control) — No auth/authz layer on any /api/knowledge/* endpoint (pre-existing, not introduced by WP-005). The GUI server binds to localhost only (port 3420) and has no token authentication. This is a known, intentional design for a local developer tool — same exposure level as the rest of the API surface. No new access control gaps introduced by WP-005 handlers. Info only.

A03 (Injection) — Path traversal defence is correctly layered: (1) KnowledgeMoveBodySchema applies PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX (/^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*$/) to both source_project_slug and project_slug at the Zod parse boundary, before any storage call. (2) KnowledgeStoreManager._validateSlug() re-checks the same regex at the storage layer (defence-in-depth). (3) The global slug used by handlePromoteKnowledge never reaches the filesystem as a path segment — it routes to the fixed globalStorePath(). No injection surface identified.

A04 (Insecure Design) — Non-atomic two-store operation: handlePromoteKnowledge and handleMoveKnowledge use add-first-then-delete across two separate KnowledgeStoreManager.withLock() calls. Each call acquires the knowledgeDir lock independently, meaning another concurrent request could observe the insight in both stores between the add and delete. This is a TOCTOU window — low exploitability in a localhost single-user tool, but worth noting. The handlers correctly surface errors from the delete phase. A fully atomic cross-store move would require a single withLock() span covering both stores. Recommend documenting as a known limitation or addressing in a follow-up WP with a cross-store transaction helper. Severity: Medium (exploitable only under concurrent requests, no data loss — just transient duplication).

A05 (Security Misconfiguration) — CORS in server.ts is correctly restricted to http://localhost:{port} (same-origin). Security headers (X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, CSP) are applied on all JSON responses via securityHeaders(). CSP uses 'unsafe-inline' for scripts and styles — pre-existing, not introduced by WP-005. No misconfiguration introduced.

A02 (Cryptographic Failures) — No secrets, credentials, tokens, or sensitive PII introduced by WP-005. The Insight schema fields (title, content, tags, source, confidence) are user-managed knowledge data stored as plain JSON on the local filesystem — consistent with the existing knowledge store design. No cleartext credential or key management concern.

A09 (Security Logging & Monitoring Failures) — Neither handlePromoteKnowledge nor handleMoveKnowledge emits any audit log on success or failure. This is consistent with the rest of the api.ts handlers (no structured audit trail anywhere in the GUI layer). Not a regression introduced by WP-005. For a localhost dev tool the risk is low; if the tool ever serves multi-user environments, audit logging for mutating operations (promote/move/delete) would be recommended.
A06 (Vulnerable & Outdated Components) — No new third-party dependencies introduced by WP-005. Uses Zod (already a project dependency) for schema validation. No CVE surface added.

No security findings — all OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed (A01–A10). No Critical or High issues identified. The two new handler functions are well-structured, rely on validated inputs via Zod schemas before any filesystem access, and delegate to a storage layer with defence-in-depth slug validation and atomic writes.

comments.note: handleMoveKnowledge (api.ts ~L1974): removed dead-code intermediate variables `sourceIsGlobal` and `sameScope`, and eliminated the empty `if (sourceIsGlobal) { /* no-op comment */ } else if (sameSlug)` control-flow construct. Replaced with two flat, independent guard clauses: (1) `if (source_scope === 'project' && !source_project_slug)` — the required-field check, now first; (2) `if (source_scope === 'project' && source_project_slug === project_slug)` — the identity check, now second. Logic is semantically equivalent (sameSlug could never be true when source_project_slug is undefined, so the reorder has no behavioral effect), but the new form is easier to read, has no unused bindings, and eliminates the need for the eslint-disable comment. All 68 tests pass.

Security Auditor flagged that when the promote/move routes are wired in server.ts (WP-002), they should follow the SAFE_SLUG_REGEX guard pattern used by other mutating routes for any URL path segments. Note: PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX (used in KnowledgeMoveBodySchema for body slugs) is intentionally wider than SAFE_SLUG_REGEX (used for URL segments) — these are different validation contexts and the difference is correct by design. The WP-002 implementor should apply SAFE_SLUG_REGEX only to URL path segments (e.g., a :slug param in the route), not to body fields which are already guarded by PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX via Zod.
